 Early voting surges with less than a week until midterm
 BY 
 Evan Koslof 
 Nationwide 
 PUBLISHED 5:24 PM ET Oct. 28, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 5:24 PM EDT Oct. 28, 2026 
 SHARE 
 As candidates begin their final sprint to election day, appearing with presidents past and present, Mike McDonald says he isn’t getting a lot of sleep.
 McDonald has been running the Election Lab at the University of Florida for close to two decades. The lab compiles data on early voting across the country.
 “It’s just me,” he said. “I’m just one person.”
 He said there has been a surge in turnout this midterm election cycle, with about 4-5 million early votes cast every day.
 As of Wednesday afternoon, nearly 40 million Americans have already voted.
 “We’re going to beat the 2022 turnout,” McDonald said. “It’s just a question of whether or not we’re going to beat the 2018 turnout.”
 McDonald said this trend is especially pronounced in Texas, where early voting is far outpacing the early voting four years ago by 1.75 million votes.
 President Donald Trump made two stops in Texas on Wednesday. The state has emerged as a key battleground with contentious races for senate and governor.
 As early voting surges, McDonald says two big trends have emerged.
 First, registered Democrats are so far outpacing registered Republicans in voting early in the roughly two dozen states that report this data. 
 But McDonald said the biggest trend he’s seeing is a spike in early voting from diverse voters.
 “There really is something going on here with Hispanics,” he said. “They’re voting at rates that are really quite eye-popping if you look at the data. I’ve never seen anything like it before.”  
 Wednesday offered another presidential split screen in the run up to the election. Trump rallied in Chillicothe, Ohio, south of Columbus, while former President Barack Obama stumped in Georgia.
 Both states are key battlegrounds with races for governor and senate.
